title: February 2026 minutes
text: February 26, 2026 Bly CATeam Attending: Leda, Lois, Quentin, Donna, Sharon, Suzanne, Nan, Rena and David. Quentin took these notes. He's pretty good at this Ai stuff. Gym Door and Window Renovations The team discussed replacing the double front doors, single side door, and two rear doors at the gym. The project will likely require reframing, and there is potential consideration of removing the middle support pending structural review. Windowless steel doors were discussed as a durable and energy-efficient option, though aesthetic preferences for glass were acknowledged. Donna will look into obtaining a quote for doors through Pacific Pine Products, while Washburn Builders would handle installation. Quentin will obtain measurements and coordinate with Washburn Builders to gather specifications and installation details. Old Gym Window Repurposing The group discussed options for approximately 32 old gym windows that were removed during upgrades. One option is to sell them individually for around $25 each through the website or Facebook. Other ideas included repurposing them for a greenhouse or community art projects. There was also consideration of offering the full lot to Miles as a bulk sale. Judicial Restitution Check Handling A restitution check in the amount of $10,454 was received from the judicial system. It was noted that there are challenges depositing the check due to it not being issued in the fire department’s name. The plan is to submit a formal request to the state to have the check reissued properly so the funds can be used for medical supplies. Fire Department Grant Applications A $2.2 million seismic rehabilitation grant application has been submitted for the fire department. If awarded, the funding would allow for a complete rebuild of both fire station buildings. Gym Insulation Grant (Stage Area) The team discussed pursuing a separate grant opportunity to install insulation under the stage area at the gym as part of ongoing facility improvements. Cookbook Sales and Promotion Ideas were shared to increase cookbook sales by offering free dessert samples from cookbook recipes at local events. The possibility of setting up a booth near the bread wagon during food sales was discussed, along with placing cookbooks at a separate, dedicated table to improve visibility and sales. Community Cleanup and Dumpster Logistics Planning is underway for the annual town cleanup event, which takes place at the beginning of May. Waste Management will provide a free dumpster, and there is consideration of arranging a separate dumpster for metal items. Placement and timing were discussed to maximize community participation and minimize misuse. Bly Area Development Opportunities The group discussed potential local development opportunities, including a daycare, bar, car wash, and storage units. Anticipated housing needs related to the proposed gold mine project were also considered, along with the broader economic and infrastructure impact that growth could bring to the community. Gym AC Unit Installation Issues Concerns were raised regarding the height placement of newly installed AC units at the gym. It was agreed that final inspection approval will be withheld until the units are raised to the agreed specifications. Issues were also noted regarding deviations from the original plan by JP and Seasons Heating and Air. Gym Website Enhancements Recent updates to the gym website were reviewed, including the addition of a “What’s Happening” section featuring live open and closed status and a member count display. A sponsors page with banner placements and an online sponsor form has been added. Rental pricing has been clarified, and a new rental application form has been implemented. Gym Financial Assistance Program The financial assistance and work exchange program has been implemented, offering five positions that require one hour of weekly cleaning in exchange for membership. Discussion included maintaining fairness and sustainability, particularly in situations where members are frequently using the facility without paying full membership fees. Gold Mine Project in Bly The proposed 15-year open-pit gold and silver mine near Quartz Mountain, along with a 35-year project near Angel’s Camp, was discussed. The project is estimated to bring a $486 million investment and create approximately 150 direct and 300 indirect jobs. Emphasis was placed on opportunities for local contractors, skilled labor positions, and broader economic benefits for the community. Gold Mine Environmental and Permitting The mine project is privately funded and not reliant on federal grants. Open-pit mining methods are planned without the use of cyanide leaching. The permitting process is expected to continue through 2026, with potential construction beginning in 2027 or 2028. Note: Personnel from the gold mine will attend our April meeting.

The Mitchell remembrance has been cancelled due to the uncertainty of the pandemic. A packet of info along with a video will be presented to the VIPs. We agreed to offer the two speakers we had contacted $100 to do a video for the package. Leda received a huge bundle of sanitizing products from TJ Maxx and will be distributing them around town. May and Kathy will not be doing the senior lunches anymore. (Thanks for the many years that you did this!) Kathy is going to talk to Donna to see if she would like to do it during the summer. Jim reported that the VA is giving the covid vaccine to veterans. Call Jim at 360-929-8866 for more information. Leda informed the group that the fire department is in the process of annexing Beatty and the surrounding area. Next CATeam meeting will be April 22 nd , 2021 . No meeting held in March because of spring break. Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: April 2021 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES April 22 , 2021 Present: Sharon Wessel, Mary Booker, Rena Melsness , Jim Lindsay , Pat Phillips, Suzanne Cornell, David Prantner and Leda Hunter We made $400 on the St. Patrick’s Day dinner. The Klamath District Garden Club (Pat & Suzanne are members) along with the community of Bly is proposing to install a Blue Star marker at the community park. This is a tribute to the armed forces that have defended the USA. Donations will be solicited to help pay for this. Pat read what will be needed at the dedication; Jim Lindsay will help with the military portion of the ceremony ; David Prantner will do the invocation. We are hoping to have the dedication on Flag Day, June 14 th 2022. Donna Kness was nominated by the team for the volunteer of the year award through the United Way. Congratulations Donna, you deserve it! Watch the newspaper on April 23 rd . Leroy Cabral, from the United Way, will attend our June meeting to see what our community needs are. They have a grant program. The Standing Stone Church is hosting a free BBQ on May 8 th to commemorate the balloon bombing that occurred in 1945. Pastor Prantner expects approximately 200 people. It was originally planned to be a potluck but the CATeam has decided to cater the event. Leda will speak with Donna Kness on the possibility that she can cater. David will speak to Donna about a tent; tables may be needed from the fire department. The town cleanup will be May 7 th with volunteers treated to lunch at the B read W agon. (Antler Grill is still closed) Meet at 9:00 am at the fire department. Bags are furnished by the CATeam. Senior lunches will be served, on Wednesday, at the B read W agon beginning in May. Cost is $5.00 for those 60 and over. A Mother’s Day brunch is planned at the site also. We usually give a welcome gift for any new business that comes to Bly. We decided to give a $50 gift certificate to the Thirsty Heifer rather than to buy a plant or something that may get stolen. Leda presented the financial statement for the last quarter. Our next meeting will be May 27 th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: May 2021 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES May 27 , 2021 Present: Sharon Wessel, Rena Melsness , Pat Phillips, Suzanne Cornell, David Prantner , Lois Michaels, Kathy Smith, Barbara Fuller and Leda Hunter We spent $700 on the Mitchell Remembrance. ($500 on BBQ, $100 on the bagpiper and $100 on the video) The application for the Blue Star Marker has been submitted. Leda asked that everyone be thinking of community needs to submit to the United Way when they attend the June meeting. The town cleanup was a huge success. We had 19 volunteers and Wayne hauled a huge load to the dump. Our permit for free dumping expired and Wayne had to pay $23. The permit has since be en reinstated (thanks Kelly Minty-Morris for your help) and he didn’t have to pay this last time. Fishing Day is June 2 nd and 3 rd at Obenchain Reservoir. Due to the pandemic it was cancelled last year so we are doing that class plus the current 4 th grade. We expect about 200 including the volunteers. Donna got one of her suppliers to donate some of the hot d ogs; she is donating the rest. We will meet at the reservoir at 10:00, begin cooking at 11:00 and serve at 11:30. Leda will pick the remaining items on June 1 st . The water rates, for the Bly customers, is going to rise on July 1 st . Rate will increase $5.00 for residential and $6.25 for commercial. Any overage over 7500 gallons will be an additional $20.00. They are holding a meeting at the gym on June 8 th at 6:30p.m. if anyone has questions. If you are inclined to sign the petition to join Idaho they will be set up at the Antler Grill on Saturday. Pat saw a bus load of older students abusing the playground equipment and will write a letter to the Paisley school. Aspen Ridge donated a $100 gift card to the preschool. We agreed to send $100 to Nate and Angie Lee to help with medical expenses while Alice is in a Portland hospital. We are going to purchase a gift certificate for plants from the Alter Society to present to Bly’s newest business; the Thirsty Heifer. A memor ial service for Larry Henderson will be held at Donna’s shop on July 17 th . A service for Sharon Jacobs will be at the gym on July 31 st . Our next meeting will be June 24 th , 2021 . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: June 2021 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES June 24 , 2021 Present: Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, David Prantner , Lois Michaels, Mary Booker , and Leda Hunter The Blue Star Marker will be here in mid-July; we can install this summer and have the celebration on Flag Day in 2022. Mary is going to ask her brother about designing the blue star for the base. We need to obtain blue rock for the design. It’s time for calendar sales again. Leda will mail out as we did last year. The company suggests that ads be sold for $150 each. We are going to leave ours at the current price of $30. We got a permit to continue free dumping for the town and park garbage. The fire department is doing a raffle for a hunting package donated by the Bly Outdoor Store. Tickets are $20 each and only 100 will be sold. Tickets are available at the Outdoor Store, the Breadwagon , and the service station or from a local firefighter. Our next meeting will be July 22 nd . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: September 2021 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES September 23 , 2021 Present: Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, Lois Michaels, Mary Booker , Rena Melsness, Kathy Forest, Donna Kness, Jim Lindsey, Kathy Smith, Kari Beckler and Leda Hunter We decided to have the annual Halloween Party on Sunday, October 31 st , from 5:00 to 7:00 pm. The following have committed: Fish Pond, Cookie Walk, Bean Bag Toss, Plinko , R ing Toss, Carmel Apples, Popcorn Balls, Water District and Photo Booth. We will check with the Forest Service to see if they want to participate. The Bootleg Fire Relief center and funding was discussed. We have received $25,570 in grants and donations since we opened in July. We decided to reimburse the fire department for the lost funding from the monthly bingo games. $150/month x 4 months =$600. We have purchased items for those affected and still have around $4,000 to spend before we close the center. Funding will be kept to pay for cleaning; the Klamath county food bank is purchasing new carpet for the fire hall. Donna has funding left from donations to the fire fighters and evacuees for meals at the Bread Wagon. We decided to hold a BBQ for the community/volunteers this fall. More info to come. We decided the Blue Star Marker would be better placed over by the lookout rather than by the highway. The fire department has a large reader board, donated from Keno fire department, which will be installed by the road that would hide the marker. The sign will be installed this fall (John Richmond) and a celebration day will be decided at a later date. Flag Day 2022 is not possible. Pat will contact Jim Lindsey on the military aspect. We are asking, on Facebook, if people feel comfortable having a Christmas program. Santa and Mrs. Santa have agreed to come on December 19 th at 6:00. Should we decide to go with having it please let Leda know so a program can be prepar ed. Jim reported that the Combat Veterans are holding a raffle; tickets are $5.00 each or 5 for $20.00. A Thanksgiving dinner will be held at the VFW at 2:00 for any veteran. They will also have a Christmas dinner on December 24 th at 2:30 . They expect to open an outreach center in Lakeview in the spring/summer of next year. The Christmas Giveaway will be at the fire hall on December 18 th from 10:00 to 2:00. All children from 0 to 18 are invited to shop for their families. We are accepting new and lightly used items. This event requires a lot of volunteers. We need personal shoppers and wrappers. Our next meeting will be October 28 th . This will be the last meeting for 2021. Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: October 2021 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES October 21 , 2021 Present: Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, Mary Booker , Donna Kness, Pat Phillips, Kari Beckler and Leda Hunter We decided the Blue Star Marker would be better placed between the two fir trees . Pat is searching for funding to pay for the concrete and has a design for the base. She has asked Walmart, Home Depot and the California garden club. The CATeam will help with expenses. We are hoping to have the ceremony on Armed Forces Day in May, 2022. The Halloween party will be October 31 st at the gym from 5:00 to 7:00 pm. We will set up at 1:00 on Sunday. Mary would like to see the graffiti removed from the building at the big corner. We could try painting over it but it is a hand hewn stone building so an acid might work better. She and her brother tried to use a power washer on it without success. Donna’s new business, Main Street Mercantile, will be open soon. ( Old Jess’s general store building) She has a committee that will decide what vendors will be allowed to display their wares. We would like to have the Christmas program at the gym again this year. If anyone would like to perform please let Leda know so she can prepare a program. The Christmas Giveaway will be at the fire hall on December 18 th from 10:00 to 2:00. All children from 0 to 18 are invited to shop for their families. We are accepting new and lightly used items. This event requires a lot of volunteers. We need personal shoppers and wrappers. Dates to Remember: Next CAT meeting: January 27th, 2022 Food Bank: 3rd Wednesday of each month Fire Department Bingo: Second Friday of each month Halloween Party: October 31st, 5:00 to 7:00 at the gym Standing Stone church ladies party: December 11th Christmas giveaway: December 18th, 11:00 to 2:00 Christmas program: December 19th, 6:00 at the gym Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: January 2020 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES January 23, 2020 Present: Lois Michaels, Bill Hudak, Karen Schlenker , Kathy Smith, Sharon Wessel, Donna Kness , Leland Hunter, David Prantner and Leda Hunter We have made $736.75 on the calendar sales. We still have a few to sell. Willie Davies and Heather Holgate received the care package from home for Christmas. Cost w as $100. The Outback church Christmas giveaway was a huge success with over 1000 gifts given out. We are collecting new and l ightly used items for next year . The bunco ladies paid for most of the refreshments; we paid $32.42. The 75 th Mitchell rededication will be held on May 5 th at the site. To pay for travel expenses for the speakers we are going to have a super bowl board and give half of the money. $10/square. Donna took the lead on this. We are also going to have a bingo on the regular night along with a silent dessert auction. Please donate a dessert! We are also planning a corned beef and cabbage dinner in March. This date will be firmed up at the next meeting. Pastor Prantner is going to do a display to honor Pastor Mitchell at the church. This will be held after the ceremony with finger foods being served. Leda will get her info on Pastor Mitchell to him. Leland said the 10 busses needed for transporting guests to the site was going to cost $12,000. If Green Diamond gave permission to use their land we could provide more parking at the site; shuttle busses and parking attendants would be needed. The next meeting for the committee is February 12 th at 1:00 at the fire hall. Margaret Jacobs will be donating for the use of the gym for Cyndi Kness memorial service. Leland says the Forest Service will be getting rid of their exercise room and would like to rent the gym from May until October each year. We agreed on $100/month; each participant will have to sign the waiver agreement. The Abiding Place church is trying to start an after school program; a meeting is set up for tomorrow. They may want to use the gym one day a week. Margaret Millen will keep me updated. Ilana Sol has published another film that will be shown at the Ross Ragland on February 28 th as a fund raiser for the county museum. It is titled Samurai in the Oregon Sky. We would like to begin having the annual target shoot if we can secure a site to do so. We shelfed this until a future meeting. Leda presented the quarterly financial report for the period ending December 31 st . Tom Crist, from the county landfill called and we scheduled May 8 th for the town cleanup. Next CATeam meeting will be February 27 th , 2020 . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: February 2020 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES February 27 , 2020 Present: Lois Michaels, Bill Hudak, Pat Phillips, Sharon Wessel, David Prantner and Leda Hunter We agreed to donate $100 to Dan & Tina Howard who lost their home to a fire. Volunteer of the year nominations are due April 2 nd . The AP church will be starting an after school program. They originally were told they could use one of the classrooms at the school but the county rescinded their offer. They asked about using the gym a couple of days a week. Quinten and I had talked about this and agreed that we would do a $20/month membership for them as long as the waivers were signed by the parents. The planning committee for the Mitchell remembrance has raised $1217 of their $2000 goal. We will have a corned beef and cabbage dinner on March 17 th at the breadwagon . Bill suggested we have a 50/50 raffle as well. We think the time will be 4:00 to 7:00 but this will be firmed up when we talk to Donna. We will be serving coffee and cookies at the Mitchell event on May 5 th . Our funding will help with this as well as finger foods for the open house at the CMA church. Open house at the church will be from 3:00 until 7:00. Pastor David offered to paint the beaver board and the coyote log if we provide the paint. Leda will purchase and get to him. Bill and Wayne will take down the eagles on the perch so Leda can paint. If you he a r of any student needing community service hours for their senior project we need to paint the inside of the restrooms. The Klamath District Garden Club is going to purchase a Blue Star marker to be placed in our community park. We agreed to partner with them; entails purchasing cement to create a star at the base, digging the hole, locating lines and spearheading a dedication ceremony when it is installed. Jim Lindsey may be able to help with military involvement. We decided to change the town cleanup to May 1 st so it is done before the Mitchell ceremony. We will notify Tom Crist of the change. Quinten plans to be home March 15 th . The band Fat Sexy will be at the gym on April 18 th . Next CATeam meeting will be April 23 rd , 2020 . No meeting in March due to spring break. Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: July 2020 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES July 23 , 2020 Present: Pat Phillips, Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, David Prantner , Terri Nixon, Mary Booker, Donna Kness, Kelly Minti -Morris and Leda Hunter Commissioner Morris has been appointed as liaison and we welcomed her to the group. This is o ur first meeting since February due to the pandemic. Revision to the notes sent out in April; we received a donation after the St. Patrick’s Day dinner for a total of $619. We now have $1832 earmarked for the Mitchell remembrance. We will pay $500 for travel expense for the speakers, assist with costs for the CMA church reception and serve cookies and beverages at the event. General consensus, by our group, is to postpone the Mitchell celebration until May 5 th of next year. Leda relayed this info to the planning committee and an email came out shortly thereafter with the decision to do so. Karen Schlenker and her daughter painted the interior of restrooms and has been doing the weekly cleaning as well. Pastor David painted the Beaver board and new letters have been installed on the entrance sign. Thanks to all of you! We have collected $370 in the RV donation can so far this month. We decided to mail out the calen dar sales this year; Leda will get this done. The Assembly of God church was closed in March and will be put on the market with an asking price of $75 to $100,000. They offered to sell it to the congregation for $50,000. The fire hall is currently being used on Sunday for church. They will give us back the clinic building that we gave to them. This was given to them so that they would have adequate parking. Our Christmas giveaway items can be stored there so we are once again collecting new and lightly used items. We decided t he Abiding Place Christian Academy will be allowed to use the building for school if they pay the utilities and build a front porch. We will have to carry liability insurance on it. Since we are a nonprofit we don’t have to pay taxes. When we purchased the Bly gym (for $1.00) we had to pay a fee to the county for the tax free status. Commissioner Boyd said we shouldn't have to pay and would check on reimbursement. (We never heard anything more) Kelly offered to help us with this if it comes up when we file the title. Leda passed around the CUP for the storage unit that is going to be built downtown. (The site of the old Pastime Tavern) The financial statement for the last quarter was presented; it’s time to do the annual taxes. Senior lunches are being served at the Bread Wagon since the school has been closed. Thanks Donna! She is also doing drive in movies that have been well attended. Free popcorn! Next CATeam meeting will be August 27 th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: September 2020 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES September 24 , 2020 Present: Pat Phillips, Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, David Prantner , Mary Booker, Donna Kness, Kathy Smith and Leda Hunter Donna found an insurance company (United S t ates Liability Insurance Co.) that will insure the gym for $2496 per year which will save us about $5000. Thanks Donna! The taxes for the years 19-20 have been filed. The Mitchell remembrance has been rescheduled for May of 2021; this could change. Calendar sales are coming in. Still have a few that indicated they want it but haven’t paid. We will have Donna and the bread wagon as the photo on the cover as volunteer of the year. Leda will ask Dave Wilson to take the photo. We now have the title for the “clinic” property and mobile home. Leda spoke with Nathan from the assessor’s office. We do have to pay the $250 fee so that we don’t have to pay property tax . The fee is a state mandate. The application and check have been mailed. The AP Christian Academy is using the clinic for their schooling program. They had to get a permit for the power meter and replace some of the water pipes. They were told that we have zero dollars to invest in the property. Leda and Margaret Millen signed a contract that stated they are responsible for all utilities, required to build a front porch and water/mow the lawn surrounding the building. We will also be allowed to store our Christmas giveaway items in one of the rooms. The Giveaway will be at the fire hall on December 12 th . We will obtain liability insurance when the porch is built. (Will send photos to the company insuring the gym) The roof on the gym is finally done. We are concerned that the e a ves won’t get boxed in before bad weather sets in. We will have to purchase some 2”x6”s but can use the plywood we have on the bottom of the eave. We discussed hiring Robert Tucker but want to have Quentin on board before we move forward. The permit expires in December. Quentin is currently working 7days a week. We are going to go ahead with the town Halloween party at the gym on October 31 st . We will post on Facebook to see if anyone wants to participate; we’re hoping everyone who had a booth last year will do so again and that Tami Nixon will do refreshments. Party will be from 6:00 to 7:30. The Christmas program at the gym is scheduled for December 18 th at the gym. We will try to organize a program again this year; we felt that helped. A memorial service will be held on October 10 th at the fire hall for Dale Jones. We will send Doris Hicks $100 to help with expenses while Keith is in the hospital. (Has been there since July 29 th ) Next CATeam meeting will be October 29th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: October 2020 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES October 29 , 2020 Present: Pat Phillips, Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, Barbara Fuller, Mary Booker, Donna Kness, Karen Schlenker and Leda Hunter Calendars will be delivered today. We are making a profit of only $431.23. We lost several advertisements this year. We will have 5 extra to sell. We have been getting quite a bit of vandalism in the park restrooms. Karen is doing a wonderful job of cleaning and Wayne repairs things as they come up. The eaves on the gym are complete. Quentin wants to put some caulking around them before he calls for the final inspection. He has been working on refurbishing the windows. Permit expires in December. The billing for the banners will go out in January. The Halloween party will be from 5 to 7:00 pm on the 31 st . The tarps will be down the morning of the event. We are hesitant to advertise it on Facebook in case someone w ants to turn us in. We expect less than 100 people . The Bly 4-H club has been distributing the farmer to family’s food boxes all summer. We all agreed to donate $100 to them to show our appreciation. Leda will send check and thank you card. We want to have a written program available for the Christmas program this year to be held on December 18 th at the gym. Please let Leda or Donna know if you plan to perform. Chrissy will need candy donations. Leda called the assessor’s office regarding the property tax bill we got for the clinic site. The form we filled out was for the next year. ( Has to be submitted before June) but they waived the taxes for this year. We need to file under 307.130 instead of as a 501c3. She will email the form to us so we can redo it. Veterans can ride free on public transportation with an ID card that you can get at the Veterans office. We are collecting new and lightly used items for the Christmas giveaway to be held on December 12 th at the fire hall. Contact Leda or Linda Gerdes (541-891-2488) with donations. Donna is setting up vendors at her shop the week after Thanksgiving. It will be open from 11:00 to 5:00, Tuesday through Sunday. She is planning an open house one evening. The Abiding Place church is having their Christmas event at the gym on December 5 th . Donna has plans for an Amazing Race event to be held late spring of 2021. This is the last meeting of the year. Next CATeam meeting will be January 28 th , 2021 . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: January 2019 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES January 24, 2019 Present: Sharon Wessel, Bill Hudak, Margaret Paulson, Quentin Nichols, Lois Michaels, Pat Phillips, Mary Booker, Steve Prince, Joel Morris, Leland Hunter and Leda Hunter Steve and Joel presented their proposal to change the road going into the gym to the south entrance and close the current access . Their plan is to eventually reconstruct the old portion of the church and add additional parking at the rear of the building. Fire chief Hunter stressed that fire vehicles have to be able to negotiate the corners. After a question and answer se ssion all agreed to the change; expected to begin this spring/summer. Leland was approached by the county sheriff recently regarding us not having an ambulance service. Leland agreed to hold a community meeting to see if there is interest before moving forward. Volunteer drivers and EMTs will be needed and funding to pay expenses. Training could be acquired through on-line courses at the fire hall. Meeting will be held on January 29 th at 6:00 p.m. at the fire hall. Leda and Mary attended the Resource Advisory Committee (RAC) meeting recently in Klamath Falls. The discussion was to change the water rules to affected wells that are closer than 500’ to the river which would allow us to irrigate this summer. The water district got a grant to drill a new well and will be moving forward with the plan. The draft letter from the state water master was given to all attendees. Leda applied for a grant from US bank for $10,000 for the gym. We will know more at the end of the month. The gym currently owes the CATeam $1501.44. Insurance is due in August $6500. The gym is offering a one month free membership for furloughed government employees. The fire department auxiliary is going to provide a meal, and a time to visit, next week. Leland says there are approximately 30 employees in Bly. We will sponsor the donkey basketball game, at the gym, on March 18 th at 7:00 pm. Concessions will be available and a dessert auction will be held at half time. Anyone wishing to donate a dessert can contact Quentin or Leda. Tickets are $1.00 cheaper is purchased before the event. Posters will be up soon. The Bly parade will be held on June 15 th . Margaret will obtain the permits and Amber Hammond will contact vendors again this year. The band, Fat Sexy, will be at the gym that night. We received a thank you from Randy and Sharon Maddock for the $1000 we donated to them. Steve mentioned that a lot of Lakeview folks stop at the community park and use the restrooms but we don’t have hand soap available. We used to have soap dispensers but they were destroyed by patrons . We do provide bars of soap when we have it. Steve thinks the church may be able to help with this. Wayne replaced the flag rope with cable so that is can’t be cut as easily. We received $141 in donations to replace the stolen flag. The fire department got a grant to replace the security camera and the area is covered now with fully functional cameras. Next meeting will be February 28 th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: April 2019 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES April 25 , 2019 Present: Margaret Paulson, Quentin Nichols, Mary Booker, Steve Prince, Joel Morris, Kathy Smith , Donna Kness and Leda Hunter The ambulance advisory board has not decided who will be awarded the ASA for the Bly area. The American Medical Association applied for the area. I will let everyone know when I hear from them. Someone turned us in for not having a permit to put the new roof on the gym. ( We didn’t know that one was needed. ) Quentin had Bill Brown help him draw up the plan. Quentin and Donna will take it to the building department. We had a request from a local person who wanted to rent the gym on Sundays to hold church services. After a lengthy discussion we decided this would be unfair to those having a membership to the facility. Leda will write a letter for Quentin to give to them. It was suggested they rent the fire hall such as the Abiding Place church did for several months. We made $2300 on the donkey basketball game. The desert auction brought in a substantial amount along with the concession stand. Kevin Newman won the 50/50 and donated most of it back. We need to send Sheila Merkley a thank you for donating the oranges that we sold. We made $660 ; Donna will get the address to Leda. We have the permits for the June 15 th parade; Margaret says Amber Hammond is lining up vendors again this year. Several offered to donate for prizes for the children participants. Give any donation to Margaret. We also discussed possibly having a community BBQ that day. Dave Wilson has agreed to be the announcer again this year. The Outback Assembly of God has purchased a trailer for collecting cans as a fund raiser. Donna suggested they have it at the auction on May 25 th . The church is also going to donate liquid soap to be placed in the restrooms at the park. Town cleanup will be Friday May 10 th beginning at 9:00 am at the fire hall. Bags will be provided and volunteers will be treated to lunch at the café. The fire department will be holding an open house on May 18 th from 11:00 to 2:00. Burgers and hotdogs will be served. ( Left over hotdogs will be used for fishing day) The fire department was formed in 1979; they are celebrating their 40 th anniversary. Assistant fire chief, Bruce N ichols, who is retiring in July, has dedicated 40 years. Fire chief Leland Hunter has been on the department for 30 years. Fishing day at Obenchain reservoir will be May 30 th . We will meet at the reservoir at 10:00 and begin cooking hotdogs at 11:00. We are expecting 85 students and around 40 volunteers. Lakeview will provide the drinks and Kathy and Sharon will make cookies. Dress warm just in case… Next meeting will be May 23 rd . The Forest Service has the fire hall reserved for that day so we may change our location. I’ll send an email to let folks know. Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: May 2019 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES May 23 , 2019 Present: Quentin Nichols, Steve and Audra Prince, Kathy Smith , Sharon Wessel, Suzanne Cornell, Bill Hudak, Lois Michaels, Pat Phillips, Derrick DeGroot and Leda Hunter Derrick DeGroot is now the liaison for our CATeam. (Please don’t quit Kathy; we love having lunch with our girlfriends) Katie Prantner is the director of the food bank taking over for Velma. The St. James Alter Society is having their annual plant sale this weekend. Thanks everyone who showed up for town cleanup. Huge success! Next meeting June 27 th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter

title: June 2019 minutes
text: BLY COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM MINUTES June 27 , 2019 Present: Quentin Nichols, Suzanne Cornell, Bill Hudak, Lois Michaels, Pat Phillips, Michelle Durant, Barbara Fuller, Mary Booker and Leda Hunter Leda gave an update on the insurance for the CAT/gym. Anyone using the gym needs to sign a waiver. The waiver was approved by the insurance company. We had to purchase insurance for the parade: $266. (Mary suggested we have a fund raising event for the parade but Margaret indicated that she didn’t want to do it anymore.) T he concert insurance is $100/ yr and weight room. $17/yr. Anyone holding a special event will have to go to www.eventhelper.com and name the CATeam as additional insured. Someone flipped the outside breaker and the doors opened. The panel is now locked. title: February 2017 minutes
text: Bly Community Action Team Notes February 23, 2017 Present: Bill Hudak , Mel Wilson, Amber Kondrato, Lois Michaels, Leda Hunter , Pat Phillips, Margaret Paulson, Donna Kness , Kathy Smith, Sharon Wessel and Leland Hunter Donnie Boyd has been assigned as our county contact. We will send him a SPECIAL invitation to the next meeting. Hopefully he will begin attending as well as our past commissioners. We discussed the fitness room at the gym that we reviewed at our last meeting. The door can be locked between the fitness room and the rest of the gym to limit trespassing. We decided to keep the monthly fee low enough that people can afford to use it. All agreed that $15.00 per month would help with utility fees. We also approved purchasing a key lock for the door and each paid person would be assigned a number ; if their monthly fee i sn’t paid their number will be locked out of the system. Leda wants to check with Quentin before we go ahead with this. Quentin is in charge of renting and scheduling use of the facility. Amber will price a keypad and let us know the cost. Mel will be retiring July 1 st after serving as an EMT for 42 years. When Mel retires we will only have one EMT. It was suggested that we put a notice in the post office to see if we can recruit potential candidates for the ambulance and the fire department. KCC did not offer the EMT course this winter term. The preschool end of year program will be April 6 th at 7:00 pm ; everyone is welcome to attend. We all agreed to help with sending Amber Kondrato to a grant writing session. The fire department will assist with the cost also. She has been taking some on line courses already and will let us know when a training session becomes available. The target shoot this year, tentatively scheduled for September 23 rd , will donate all proceeds to Randy Maddock. He has cancer, no insurance and no income. We agreed to May 12 th for the town cleanup. We would like to encourage some of the local residents to clean up around their homes and will ask Klamath county official, Tom Crist, if it would be possible to allow free dumping for residents rather than just for roadside cleanup. In the past free dumping is for yard debris only. St. James Alter Society will not be holding the fish fry this year but will instead hold a plant sale on Memorial Day weekend. Gift certificates can be purchased ahead of time for Mother’s day. Fishing Day will be June 1 st this year. They expect 80 students plus volunteers; this means we need to purchase extra hotdogs. Any left over hotdogs can be saved for the target shoot. Leland expressed concern regarding the fire department being expected to respond to Beatty and Sprague River. Leland was assigned as Incident Commander for the recent flood event and the Bly fire department was expected to cover these areas that are not within our assigned area. The fire department collects taxes on 7 square miles but is expected to respond to a 106 square mile area. We often respond to Beatty and even though we are allowed to bill them for our services most people do not have insurance and we seldom collect any funds. Leda explained that fire chief, Leland Hunter, has worked long and hard to bring the department up to national standards. We will soon be having an ISO inspection that hopefully will decrease our fire rating. We are currently at a rating of 6 and hope to get to a 5 or possibly a 4. This rating will reduce insurance costs for our residents. It would help if we had a designated landing zone for transporting medical patients by helicopter. The pad needs to be approximately 20’x20’ and needs to have ambulance access and no close by power lines. If we can get land donated we can hold a fund raising event to pay for the concrete. The Easter egg hunt will be hosted by the fire department on April 16 th at 2:00 pm at the school. The Altar Society offered to purchase 15 dozen eggs. We will not have a CATeam meeting in March due to spring break. The next meeting will be April 27 th . Respectfully submitted, /s/Leda Hunter
